hints: The dims you pass are the ones that disappear.

title: Standardising channels
description: Standardises each channel of an image batch: subtract the channel mean and divide by the channel standard deviation, using broadcasting only.
code:
def normalize_channels(x, mean, std):
    # x: (N, C, H, W); mean, std: (C,)
    mean = mean.reshape(1, -1, 1, 1)
    std = std.reshape(-1, 1, 1, 1)
    return (x - mean) * std

errors.explanation: std must have the same (1, C, 1, 1) layout as mean, otherwise it lines up with the batch axis instead of the channel axis.
Standardisation divides by the standard deviation; multiplying makes the result wrong.

hints: The two parameters should be reshaped the same way.
Check the shape of std against mean, then the arithmetic operator.
Line 4 needs (1, -1, 1, 1); line 5 needs a division.

title: CIFAR-10 bytes to images
description: Turns a (N, 3072) uint8 CIFAR-10 matrix, stored as 1024 red values, then 1024 green values, then 1024 blue values per row, into a float32 batch of shape (N, 3, 32, 32) scaled to [0, 1].
code:
def raw_to_images(raw):
    raw = torch.tensor(raw)
    N = raw.shape[0]
    images = raw.reshape(N, 32, 32, 3)
    images = images.to(torch.float32)
    images = images // 255
    return images

errors.explanation: Each row is channel-major (all reds, then greens, then blues), so the reshape must be (N, 3, 32, 32), not channel-last.
// is floor division: every pixel below 255 becomes 0. Use true division to scale into [0, 1].

hints: Think about how the 3072 numbers are laid out inside one row.
Two lines are wrong: one about the target shape, one about the scaling operator.
Channel axis comes first: (N, 3, 32, 32); and use / instead of //.

title: Nearest-mean classifier as a linear layer
description: Converts class templates mu_k into the weights of a linear classifier. The score -0.5*||x-mu_k||^2 equals x . mu_k - 0.5*||mu_k||^2 up to a term that is the same for every class, so W holds the templates and b the squared-norm penalty.
code:
def nearest_mean_params(means):
    # means: (K, D)  ->  W: (D, K), b: (K,)
    W = means
    b = 0.5 * (means ** 2).sum(dim=1)
    return W, b

errors.explanation: scores = X @ W needs W of shape (D, K); means is (K, D), so transpose it.
The bias is MINUS half the squared norm: farther-from-origin templates must be penalised, not rewarded.

hints: Check the shapes needed for X @ W + b, then the sign in the derivation.
Expand -0.5*||x - mu||^2 and keep only the terms that depend on k.
W = means.T and b = -0.5 * ||mu_k||^2.

title: Cross-entropy in the log domain
description: Mean cross-entropy computed from raw scores without any forbidden helper: shift for stability, get log-probabilities of every class, pick the correct class of each row, and average the negative values.
hints: log softmax(z)_k = z_k - log(sum_j exp(z_j)); never form softmax first.
For the second blank you need, per row, the entry whose column index is the label.
torch.gather(log_probs, 1, labels.reshape(-1, 1)) (or advanced indexing with torch.arange).
explanation: Working with log-probabilities avoids exp underflow -> 0 -> log(0) = -inf. gather along dim 1 with a (N,1) index picks log p[i, labels[i]] for every row.

title: Picking the best temperature
description: Tries each temperature T, divides the scores by T and keeps the first T that gives the lowest cross-entropy. Predictions never change with T; only the loss does.
